edges.notes: Debian ships Linux kernel packages for supported architectures as part of the distribution.
Debian GNU/Linux userland on standard ports uses glibc as the C library alongside the dynamic linker.
systemd is the default init system on current Debian stable releases per Debian documentation.
Debian services are expressed as systemd unit files and drop-ins on default systemd installs.
Debian userland binaries and shared libraries are ELF on typical Linux targets.
GCC toolchain packages are central to Debian build-essential and package build flows.
GNU binutils participate in standard Debian package build and link flows.
g++-built packages link GNU libstdc++ above glibc on typical Debian GNU/Linux flows.
Clang/LLVM packages are available from Debian archives for alternative compiler stacks.
Official debian and debian:slim OCI images are common bases; Docker pulls and runs them like other Linux images.
CRI/containerd nodes run Debian-based workload images pulled as OCI artifacts.
Kubernetes nodes and pods frequently use Debian-class images on Linux; not exclusive.
Debian bases are packaged as OCI image rootfs layers conforming to OCI image layout conventions.
Substitutable Linux distribution defaults for containers and servers (glibc/systemd vs musl/OpenRC field patterns).
Ubuntu derives packaging heritage and archive practices from Debian with independent governance and release cadence.
